data.title: [ACT5] 2,364 activities are stuck open with no date - 60% of leads show a next step that is really old history
data.description:
BUG - measured across all of production, 28 July, after Kim reported the Maranatha lead showing warnings that made no sense.

THE NUMBERS Of everything the CRM currently treats as outstanding, 2,364 items carry NO date at all and only 193 are genuine dated next steps. So 92% of the 'outstanding' work is old history that was never closed. It sits on 898 of 1,497 leads - 60% of the pipeline - and 815 of those leads have NO real next step at all, meaning what the screen shows them as their next step is entirely this unclosed history.

WHAT THEY ACTUALLY ARE Records of work already done, written in the previous CRM's style - 'Call: No answer', 'Call: In a meeting', 'WhatsApp: She forwarded fliers'. The old system had no way to close an entry, so reps logged what happened and moved on. Those habits carried over.

SPREAD BY OWNER Tanya 382 leads / 664 items, Manake 188 / 649, Kim 48 / 479, unassigned 172 / 334, busi 106 / 191. Kim's are the most concentrated - about ten per lead, which is why Maranatha looked so cluttered.

IT IS NOT ONLY LIVE WORK 571 items sit on disqualified leads and 141 on converted ones - closed business still generating open items and SLA warnings.

IT IS STILL HAPPENING Only 32 items are older than six months; 1,508 are one to three months old and 193 are from the last month. This is current practice, not a legacy dump, so cleaning up without changing the forms means it refills at roughly 500 a month.

WHAT THIS BREAKS Every SLA warning, idle-lead alert, hygiene score and discipline figure built on 'open activities' is reading this noise as real commitments.

WHAT IS NEEDED (1) Fix the forms so a rep logging work already done records it as done, not as an open undated item - see [ACT2] and [NEXT2]. (2) Then close the backlog at database level, dating each item by its own date. It CANNOT be done through the Done button until [ACT4] is fixed, or it will restamp 898 leads as contacted today.

data.title: [ACT4] Marking an old activity done rewrites the lead's contact date to today
data.description:
BUG - proven on production 28 July on the Maranatha Christian Schools lead (Kim's).

WHAT HAPPENS Mark any old activity as done and the system records it as completed TODAY, then pushes that date onto the lead as its last contact. On the lead we tested, a call logged on 3 July was marked done and the lead's last-contact date jumped from 3 July to 28 July - on a lead that is DISQUALIFIED. One click, one record.

WHY IT MATTERS Reps and managers tidying up old activities will silently destroy the contact history of every lead they touch. Last-contact dates drive the SLA warnings, the idle-lead alerts and the hygiene score, so a stale lead that somebody tidies up starts looking freshly worked. This is not a bulk-script problem - it happens through normal everyday use of the Done button.

SECOND FAULT FOUND WITH IT Putting the activity back to scheduled does NOT clear the completion time. The record then reads as scheduled while still carrying a completion date and outcome, so the damage cannot be undone from the screen.

WHAT IS NEEDED When an activity is completed, the completion date should be the date the work actually happened - the activity's own date where it has one, or ask the person when it was - rather than always the moment the button was pressed. And reverting a completion must clear the completion date, outcome and note.

BLOCKS the clean-up of the 2,364 stuck activities in [ACT5]: that clean-up cannot go through this route until this is fixed, or it will restamp 898 leads as contacted today.

data.title: [SCHLEAD2] Create a lead from a school that has none - inheriting the school's details, and NOT named after the school
data.description:
FEATURE - specified 28 July, extends SCHLEAD1. Now that the import brings in schools WITHOUT leads (as intended - the sales team creates the lead when the school is assigned to them, by a manager or by the routing engine), there is no way to start one from the school page. A rep opening a school with no lead reaches a dead end.

WHAT IS NEEDED When a school has no lead, the school page must say so plainly and offer 'Create lead'. Choosing it opens the new-lead form with everything already known about the school carried across, so nobody retypes it: the school itself, its town, province and region, and the head as the primary contact with their phone number.

THE LEAD NAME MUST NOT BE THE SCHOOL NAME. That is the mistake behind LNAME1, where 94 leads ended up named after their school. A lead is what the school is buying - for example 'Interactive Boards' - not who they are. The school is already recorded on the lead; repeating it as the name loses the only field that says what the opportunity actually is. The form should either ask for the opportunity or offer the usual product options.

WHO IT AFFECTS Every rep working the 368 imported schools, and every school added from now on.

NOT STARTED - queued at the owner's request pending Mr Dube's answer. No changes made.

data.title: [IMPORT2] Imported schools show no principal and no phone number, although the file had both
data.description:
BUG - reported 28 July. WHAT YOU SEE Open one of the 368 newly imported schools and the Principal is blank and there is no phone number on the school, even though the source file supplied the head's name, surname and number for almost every one.

WHY The import saved that person as a CONTACT under the school, which is correct and the details are there - for example Nyandoro Secondary has the contact Kudzai Maporisa, Head, 771507239. But the school record itself has its own separate 'principal name' and 'phone' fields, and the import never filled those. So the school page and the schools list look empty while the information sits one level down on the contact.

WHAT IT AFFECTS All 368 imported schools. The schools list shows a Principal column, so the whole list reads as though we imported schools with no contact details at all - which is the opposite of the truth and undermines confidence in the import.

WHAT IS NEEDED Copy the head's name and number from the contact up onto the school record for every imported school, so the Principal and phone show where people look for them. Going forward the import should set both at the same time. Worth deciding at the same time whether the school's principal field should simply follow the contact marked Head, rather than being a second place the same fact is stored - two copies of one fact will drift apart.

NOT STARTED - queued at the owner's request pending Mr Dube's answer. No changes made.

data.title: [METRICS1] The dashboard numbers measure the wrong things - audit of every figure
data.description:
AUDIT, 28 July. Several figures across the dashboards do not measure what their labels say. None of them fail visibly - each returns a confident, plausible, wrong number, which is worse. Checked against production and against the pristine copy of the previous CRM.

WHAT IS WRONG

1. Qualification panel. It reads 'Total leads 2,419' when there are 1,753 leads. It is counting qualification FORM RECORDS, not leads - some leads have three, and the 443 leads with no record at all are invisible. The 'average score 4.2' is out of 100, not out of 5, and is dragged down by empty duplicate records. The panel cannot be read as how well the pipeline is qualified.

2. Daily contact target (40). It counts leads whose FIRST EVER contact happened today, not calls made. A rep making 40 calls to leads they have already spoken to scores zero. Five calls to the same school count as one. A WhatsApp counts the same as a call. On the team view the target is 40 multiplied by every active user, including admins and finance, rather than by the number of reps. There is no manager target of 10 anywhere in the system.

3. Deals list. It returns only ongoing deals and says nothing about it - two thirds of deals (won and lost) are invisible to anything built on that list. Raised separately as DEALS1.

4. Quotes. Only one quote has ever expired; 17 have no validity date so they never can; 20 belong to no deal so they are invisible to every pipeline and forecast. Raised separately as QUOTE2, QUOTE3, QUOTE6.

5. Currency. Deals are a mix of rand and dollars, and quotes carry no currency at all - a quote total is a bare number with nothing saying what it is in. Note this corrects QUOTE4, which says every deal is rand.

6. 93 activities are marked completed but carry no completion time, so every measure keyed on that date silently skips them.

WHAT IS SOUND: the SLA breach figures, the lead status spread, and the Nurture status are all correct and can be relied on.

NOT YET CHECKED: funnel health, demo statistics, lead conversion, top products, schools bought, nurture follow-ups, collections due.

Full working in METRICS-AUDIT.md in the codebase. The first decision needed is what '40 a day' should mean - calls made, or new leads opened. They are different measures and the fix differs.
data.resolution_note: DECISION FROM MR DUBE, 28 July. '40 a day' means ANY activity completed that day - including calls to leads already being worked. It is a measure of effort, not of discovery. New leads touched keeps its own separate SLA measure, AND contacting a new lead also counts toward the 40. Both are to be tracked: new leads contacted and existing leads contacted. His words: 'Yes, any new activity done on the day. New leads touched has its own SLA, but contacting a new lead also adds to 40 a day. They'll not always be new.' WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BUILD: the figure on screen today counts only first-ever contacts, so it measures the wrong one of his two things and labels it as the other. A genuine daily activity counter is a NEW measure, not a correction of the existing one. The existing first-contact measure stays, correctly labelled, alongside its SLA. Also to fix at the same time: the team target multiplies 40 by every active user including admins and finance, rather than by the number of reps.

data.title: API discloses its technology stack via X-Powered-By header
data.description:
WHERE: NestJS/Express default (src/main.ts)

WHAT'S WRONG: Every API response includes `X-Powered-By: Express`.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: curl -I https://api.digilearncrm.work/api/v2/leads

IMPACT: Minor - tells an attacker the stack, helping them target known Express/Nest issues. Low risk on its own but free to remove.

FIX: `app.disable('x-powered-by')` in main.ts (or set `app.getHttpAdapter().getInstance().disable('x-powered-by')`).

data.title: Missing security headers on the web app (CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
data.description:
WHERE: nginx config serving the frontend

WHAT'S WRONG: The site returns none of the standard protective headers. Confirmed missing: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: curl -I https://crm.digilearncrm.work

IMPACT: The app can be framed by a malicious site (clickjacking - a rep could be tricked into clicking real CRM buttons), MIME-sniffing is not blocked, and referrer data leaks to third parties.

FIX: Add to the nginx server block: X-Frame-Options DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, a Content-Security-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security.

data.title: Session cookie Secure/SameSite flags depend on NODE_ENV being set in the container
data.description:
WHERE: src/auth/auth.controller.ts:35-45

WHAT'S WRONG: `const IS_PRODUCTION = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` drives `secure: IS_PRODUCTION` and `sameSite: IS_PRODUCTION ? 'none' : 'lax'`. If the deployed container does not set NODE_ENV=production, the refresh-token cookie loses its Secure flag (so it can travel over plain HTTP - see the plaintext HTTP bug) and SameSite=lax would break the cross-subdomain refresh between crm.* and api.*.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Check the running container's environment. Then log in and inspect the crm_auth.session_token cookie flags in DevTools.

IMPACT: Potential session-token exposure over plaintext, or refresh failures causing unexpected logouts.

FIX: Confirm NODE_ENV=production is set in the deployment. Safer: derive these flags from an explicit config value that fails closed (default to secure) rather than from NODE_ENV.

data.title: API documentation is publicly exposed in production
data.description:
WHERE: src/main.ts (Swagger/Scalar setup, no environment gate)

WHAT'S WRONG: The full interactive API reference is reachable with no authentication in production.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Open https://api.digilearncrm.work/api/v2/docs in a private browser window - the complete endpoint catalogue, parameters and schemas are listed.

IMPACT: Hands an attacker a map of every endpoint and payload shape, which materially speeds up abuse of the auth and access-control bugs in this log.

FIX: Only mount the docs when NODE_ENV !== 'production', or put them behind admin authentication / an allowlisted IP.

data.title: No brute-force protection on login - unlimited password attempts
data.description:
WHERE: src/auth (no throttler/rate-limit guard on the login route)

WHAT'S WRONG: I sent 8 consecutive failed logins against production; all returned a plain 401 with no throttling, no delay and no 429. There is per-account lockout logic, but no IP/request-level rate limiting, so an attacker can cycle many accounts or run distributed guessing.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Repeatedly POST /api/v2/auth/login with wrong credentials - no rate limiting kicks in.

IMPACT: Password-guessing and credential-stuffing are unimpeded.

FIX: Add @nestjs/throttler (or an nginx rate limit) on the auth routes - e.g. 5-10 attempts per IP per minute with exponential backoff - and log/alert repeated failures.

data.title: Site and API both work over plain HTTP - login credentials can be sent unencrypted
data.description:
WHERE: nginx config for crm.digilearncrm.work and api.digilearncrm.work

WHAT'S WRONG: http://crm.digilearncrm.work returns 200 with NO redirect to HTTPS, and http://api.digilearncrm.work also answers. I confirmed the login endpoint accepts credentials over plaintext HTTP. There is also no Strict-Transport-Security header, so browsers are never told to upgrade.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: curl -I http://crm.digilearncrm.work -> 200 (no 301). curl -X POST http://api.digilearncrm.work/api/v2/auth/login -> processes the request.

IMPACT: A rep on hotel/airport/public WiFi who types the address without https:// sends their password and session token in the clear, where they can be captured.

FIX: Add a 301 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS on both hosts and set Strict-Transport-Security (e.g. max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains).

data.title: All uploaded documents (contracts, POs, ID scans) are listable by any logged-in user
data.description:
WHERE: src/file-manager/file-manager.controller.ts:85 (and the other GET handlers)

WHAT'S WRONG: The file-manager read endpoints carry no @Roles decorator and no per-user scoping, so they fall through to the guard's default-allow for any authenticated principal.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Authenticate as ANY user of ANY role (including an account minted through the public /auth/register bug). GET /api/v2/file-manager?limit=500 -> every ManagedFile row with file_name and file_url. Fetching a file_url downloads the document with no further authentication.

IMPACT: Signed purchase orders, contracts, quote PDFs and ID scans are readable by any account, and the storage URLs appear to be unauthenticated.

FIX: Add @Roles('admin','sales_manager','sales_rep') to the GET handlers at minimum, and scope findAll/findByEntity to the caller (for a sales_rep, restrict to files whose entity resolves to a lead/deal assigned to them). Also make the storage URLs signed/expiring rather than publicly fetchable.

data.title: Bulk deal update authorizes with .some() instead of .every() - one owned deal unlocks the whole batch
data.description:
WHERE: src/deals/deals.service.ts:931

WHAT'S WRONG: The ownership guard uses .some(), so it passes if the caller owns ANY ONE deal in the submitted batch - then updates all of them in a single transaction.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: As rep A who owns exactly one deal D1, PATCH /api/v2/deals/bulk-update with [{id:D1,...},{id:B1,...},{id:B2,...}] where B1/B2 belong to rep B -> all three are re-staged and repositioned. Removing D1 from the array correctly returns 403, proving the check only requires one owned record.

FIX: Change .some() to .every(). Better: filter the batch to records the caller may touch and reject the whole request (rather than silently partially applying) if any requested id is out of scope.

data.title: Any rep can mark another rep's deal Won or Lost
data.description:
WHERE: src/deals/deals.service.ts:579 (closeDeal) and update()

WHAT'S WRONG: closeDeal and update have no ownership check at all, unlike bulkUpdate which does resolve the actor's roles.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: As rep A, PATCH /api/v2/deals/{rep B's deal}/close with {"close_status":"Lost","lost_reason":"x"} -> 200. B's live deal is closed, actualCloseDate is stamped, it drops off the pipeline board and out of B's forecast, and reversing it needs the rollback-request workflow.

IMPACT: Deal outcomes and revenue reporting can be corrupted by any rep - closing Won inflates reported revenue, closing Lost destroys a live opportunity.

FIX: Add the same authorization guard used in bulkUpdate at the top of closeDeal and update: unless the caller is admin/sales_manager, require deal.assigned_to === actorId, else throw ForbiddenException.

data.title: Any rep can edit or re-stage another rep's lead (no per-record authorization)
data.description:
WHERE: src/leads/leads.service.ts:749 (update) and the status-change handler

WHAT'S WRONG: Lead update and status-change perform no object-level authorization - they call findOne(id) without the ability, so ownership is never verified.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: As rep A, PATCH /api/v2/leads/{rep B's lead}/status with {"status":"Nurture"} -> 200. B's lead leaves the active funnel, its SLA clock and next action are rewritten, and the activity log attributes the change to A. PUT /api/v2/leads/{B's lead} with {"next_action_due_date":null} also succeeds.

IMPACT: Any rep can silently sabotage or disrupt another rep's pipeline; SLA and follow-up discipline data becomes unreliable.

FIX: Thread @CaslAbility() from both controller handlers into the service, use findOne(id, ability) in update, and add the same canReadLead/canAccessRecord gate (with Action.UPDATE) at the top of the status-change path.

data.title: Lead CSV export ignores permissions and dumps every lead in the company
data.description:
WHERE: src/leads/leads.controller.ts:136

WHAT'S WRONG: exportCsv calls `leadsService.findAll({limit:'1000'})` WITHOUT the ability argument, while the normal list endpoint passes it. Inside findAll the scoping is `if (ability) { applyScope... }` (leads.service.ts:507) - so when it is missing NO filtering is applied at all. The permission check is fail-open, not fail-closed.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: As any sales_rep, GET /api/v2/leads/export -> CSV of up to 1000 leads including school, province, contact name, phone number and owner, regardless of the rep's restrictions.

IMPACT: Full customer-list exfiltration by any rep - and, combined with the open registration bug, by anyone on the internet.

FIX: Pass the ability through to findAll from the export handler, and make the scoping fail-closed (require an ability, or default to the caller's own records when none is supplied).

data.title: Pipeline board shows every rep's deals - ownership filter silently dropped (assignedTo vs assigned_to)
data.description:
WHERE: src/deals/deals.controller.ts:119 and src/deals/deals.service.ts:371-390

WHAT'S WRONG: The controller pulls the CASL condition object, which for a sales_rep is `{ assignedTo: '<uuid>' }` (camelCase, from seed-roles-permissions.ts:133). findPipelineDeals destructures `{ status, search, assigned_to }` (snake_case). The key never matches, assigned_to is undefined, `...(assigned_to && {assigned_to})` contributes nothing, and the WHERE clause loses the ownership filter entirely.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Log in as a sales rep and open the pipeline kanban -> every ongoing deal for the whole company is returned with value, school and assigned user.

IMPACT: Silent, total loss of per-rep data isolation on the main pipeline screen. This is also how a rep discovers other reps' deal IDs to exploit the deal IDOR.

FIX: Stop hand-rolling condition extraction. Pass the AppAbility into findPipelineDeals and use AbilityScopeService.applyScopeToQueryBuilder with a DEAL_CONDITION_KEY_MAP, mirroring LeadsService.findAll (leads.service.ts:507-513).

data.title: Any rep can open any other rep's deal (ownership check is a no-op)
data.description:
WHERE: src/deals/deals.controller.ts:262

WHAT'S WRONG: The check is `ability.can(Action.READ, 'Deal') || ability.can(Action.READ, subject('Deal', data))`. The first operand passes a subject TYPE string; CASL deliberately ignores conditions for type-level checks (it answers 'can I read at least one Deal?'), which is always true for a sales_rep. The `||` short-circuits, so the per-record check never runs.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: As rep A, GET /api/v2/deals/{a deal belonging to rep B} -> 200 with full deal: value, school, contacts, stage history, quotes, invoices. Expected 403.

IMPACT: Any rep can read every deal in the company including values and commercial history.

FIX: Drop the type-level operand and check only the instance. Reuse AbilityScopeService.canAccessRecord with a DEAL_CONDITION_KEY_MAP ({assignedTo: 'assigned_to'}) exactly as leads/invoices/quotes already do (leads.service.ts:1736-1746).

data.title: Idle-lead alert repeats every 2 hours forever (~84 duplicate emails per lead per week)
data.description:
WHERE: src/sla/sla-scheduler.service.ts:378-396 and :447-453

WHAT'S WRONG: handleIdleLeadCheck looks for a suppression record with `idle_alert_sent: true`, but the ONLY place that flag is ever written is line 449, which is guarded by `if (existingHistory)`. The flag defaults to false and the history row created on status transition (leads.service.ts:1397-1408) never sets it. So existingHistory is always null, the dedupe `continue` never fires, and the flag can never become true.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Any lead idle past its idle_alert_hours threshold. The cron fires every 2 hours and each run creates a fresh notification + sends another idle-lead-alert email.

IMPACT: Reps get ~84 identical emails per idle lead per week, multiplied across their whole book. Alert fatigue means real SLA warnings get ignored.

FIX: Drop `idle_alert_sent: true` from the lookup (match on lead_id + status + exited_status_at IS NULL only), and make the write path an upsert: if no open history row exists, create one with idle_alert_sent=true and idle_alert_sent_at=now. Move the email send behind the same check.

data.title: Invoice stays 'Paid' with a paid date after its payments are removed
data.description:
WHERE: src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:804 (recalculatePaymentStatus)

WHAT'S WRONG: When total payments drop to zero the code sets payment_status='Unpaid' but never clears status='Paid' or paid_date.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Fully pay an invoice (status=Paid, paid_date set), then delete the payment. payment_status flips to Unpaid but status stays 'Paid' and paid_date stays populated.

IMPACT: GET /invoices/stats keeps counting the invoice under paidValue, so revenue and collections figures are overstated after any payment correction.

FIX: Make the zero branch symmetric: set payment_status='Unpaid', paid_date=null, and if status is 'Paid' or 'Partially-Paid' revert it to 'Sent'.

data.title: Deleting or editing a payment never reverses the installment - installment stays marked paid
data.description:
WHERE: src/payments/payments.service.ts:160 (remove) and :125-154 (update)

WHAT'S WRONG: remove() deletes the payment and only recalculates the invoice-level status. The payment_allocations rows cascade away, but nothing restores installments.paid_amount / balance / status, which allocatePaymentFIFO wrote directly (payment-terms.service.ts:778-781). update() has the same hole - changing the amount leaves allocated_amount, unallocated_amount and every credited installment frozen at the old figures.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Record a payment allocated to installment 1 (installment becomes paid_amount=4000, balance=0, status=paid). DELETE that payment. The installment STILL reads paid/4000/0 with no payment behind it.

IMPACT: A mis-posted payment that gets deleted leaves the school permanently marked as having paid - they are never chased again, and collections reporting overstates receipts.

FIX: Wrap create/update/remove in dataSource.transaction. Before deleting, load the payment_allocations and inside the same transaction decrement each installment's paid_amount, restore balance and recompute status (pending|partially_paid|paid), then delete. For update(), reverse existing allocations then re-run allocation.

data.title: CRITICAL: Payments marked fully allocated but no money is actually applied to installments
data.description:
WHERE: src/payment-terms/payment-terms.service.ts:748

WHAT'S WRONG: The code is `Number(payment.unallocated_amount || payment.amount)`. PostgreSQL numeric columns come back as STRINGS, so a new payment's unallocated_amount is the string '0.00' - which is TRUTHY in JavaScript. The `||` fallback never fires, so the allocator starts with 0 to distribute, breaks out of the loop immediately, and writes NO payment_allocations rows. Lines 793-797 then mark the payment as 100% allocated anyway.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: Record any payment against an invoice that has a payment term/installment schedule. Result: payments.allocated_amount = full amount, but 0 rows in payment_allocations and the installment still shows pending/unpaid with the full balance.

IMPACT: EVERY payment in the system. Schools that have paid are still shown as owing, get chased, and flip to overdue triggering dunning - while reports claim the money was allocated.

FIX: Never use truthiness on a decimal column. Use an explicit null check: `const raw = payment.unallocated_amount; const remaining = (raw === null || raw === undefined) ? Number(payment.amount) : Number(raw);` and set unallocated_amount = amount when the payment is created (payments.service.ts:53). Add a regression test seeding unallocated_amount as the string '0.00'.

data.title: CRITICAL: Anyone on the internet can register a working CRM account
data.description:
WHERE: src/auth/auth.controller.ts:56 (@Public + @SkipRolesCheck), src/auth/auth.service.ts:79-165

WHAT'S WRONG: The registration endpoint is public - no authentication required. It creates a user with is_active=true and assigns the 'sales_rep' role, then returns a working access token. Login never checks email_verified, so the account works immediately. There is no config switch to disable registration.

HOW TO REPRODUCE: POST https://api.digilearncrm.work/api/v2/auth/register with {email, password, first_name, last_name} from anywhere on the internet -> 201 + valid token.

IMPACT: A stranger self-provisions a sales_rep account (112 endpoints) and can read the full schools/leads/contacts database, deal values, dashboard KPIs and uploaded documents. Confirmed by 2 independent code reviews + live probe of production.

FIX: Remove @Public()/@SkipRolesCheck() from AuthController.register and gate with @Roles('admin'), or delete the route entirely - admin-only staff provisioning already exists at POST /users (users.controller.ts:108).

data.title: [DEALS1] /deals silently returns ongoing deals only - 26 closed deals (US$346,465) hidden, and the filter is close_status while the response field is closeStatus
data.description: The deals list only ever shows deals that are still running, and nothing on the screen says so — it looks like the full list. 26 closed deals worth US$346,465 are simply absent. Anyone reading it sees 6 deals when the real number is 32, so won and lost business disappears from view.

data.title: [QUOTE6] Creating a quote does not create or advance a deal - 25 of 67 quotes (US$280,363) have no deal at all, and expired quotes never mark the deal Lost
data.description: Raising a quote does nothing to the pipeline. The lead stays exactly where it was, and attaching the quote to a deal is optional — so 25 of 67 quotes, worth US$280,363, belong to no deal at all and are invisible to every pipeline and forecast. When a quote expires, the deal it belongs to is never marked lost either. Mr Dube has specified the behaviour he wants instead.

data.title: [QUOTE5] po_received looks unused - only 3 of 67 quotes have it set, including 9 Accepted quotes with no PO
data.description: The quote record has a tick for 'purchase order received', but only 3 of 67 quotes have it ticked — including 9 quotes marked Accepted with no purchase order against them. Either the orders genuinely are not arriving, or they are arriving and nobody ticks the box. Worth confirming with the team before treating the figure as real.

data.title: [QUOTE4] Deal currency is stored as ZAR but the business sells in USD - quotes carry no currency field at all
data.description: Every deal is recorded in South African rand, but the business sells in US dollars — so the currency stored against every deal is simply wrong. Quotes are worse: they carry no currency at all, just a bare number, so nothing in the record states what the amount is in.

data.title: [QUOTE3] A quote can be saved with no validity date at all - 17 of 67 have none, so they can never expire or be chased
data.description: A quote can be saved with no validity date at all, and 17 of the 67 quotes have none. Those quotes sit in a blind spot: with no date they can never lapse, so they will not be picked up even once expiry is automated, and nobody can chase them because nothing says when they run out.

data.title: [QUOTE2] Quotes never expire - 34 quotes (US$397,863) are past their validity date but still read as open
data.description: Quotes never expire. Once a quote passes its validity date nothing happens — it stays open forever, the owner is never warned it is about to lapse, and nothing on the list shows it is dead. 34 of the 67 quotes in the system, worth US$397,863, are already past their date and still read as live.

data.title: [NEXT2] The app asks for the next step AFTER marking done, but the server demands it BEFORE - reps get a 400 they cannot clear
data.description:
BUG - found 2026-07-27 when Manake could not complete an activity on the Rupare High lead ("request failed with status code 400").

What the app does: the completion dialog marks the activity done first, and only then opens the follow-up prompt asking what the next step is. That is the intended experience - do the work, say what happens next.

What the server does: with the setting 'enforce_next_step_on_completion' switched ON, the server refuses the completion unless the lead ALREADY has a future activity scheduled, or the request carries a next_step payload. The app never sends that payload - the screen that collects the next step runs after the completion has already been rejected.

So the two halves disagree. On a lead that happens to have something scheduled, the rep never notices. On a lead with an empty next-step slot - exactly where the prompt matters most - completion fails with a 400 the rep cannot clear by any action on screen. Managers and admins bypass the gate, so it looks fine to them.

The switch was turned on 2026-07-24 20:05 UTC (three compliance settings written within 300ms of each other, the signature of somebody saving the Compliance & Controls page). Settings changes are not recorded anywhere, so the system cannot say who.

Immediate fix applied: turn the setting back OFF. Discipline is not lost - the app's own follow-up prompt still requires the next step after completion.

Proper fix, pick one: (a) keep asking after completion and leave the server gate off, or (b) collect the next step inside the completion dialog and send it as the next_step payload so both halves agree, or (c) on a 400, open the follow-up prompt and retry the completion with the payload. Do not switch the setting on again until one of these ships.
data.resolution_note: Reps were unblocked within the hour on 27 July by switching off the setting that caused it, so nobody is stuck. The underlying design conflict is NOT yet fixed: the app marks an activity done first and asks for the next step afterwards, while that setting requires the next step first — and the screen never sends it. Do not switch 'require a next step on completion' back on until the follow-up box is rebuilt to send the next step together with the completion. Left in progress deliberately so the remaining work is not forgotten.

data.title: I edited a product from 85 inch to 86 inch in the products page, the change should effect change to all other areas where that was used
data.description: I edited a product from 85 inch to 86 inch in the products page, the change should effect change to all other areas where that was used
data.resolution_note:
FIXED AND LIVE ON PRODUCTION 2026-07-24 (prod-ticketing commit ecffbb7).

WHAT WAS WRONG. When a product is added to a quote or an invoice, the product's name is copied into that line as text and stored there, with a link back to the product. Renaming the product changed the product record and nothing else, so every line that had already been written kept saying "85 Inch Interactive Board".

WHAT WAS DONE. Renaming a product now also updates the lines on DRAFT quotes and invoices, so they follow the new name. Only lines still carrying the exact old wording are touched — if someone has typed over a line by hand, it is left as they wrote it.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED. Documents that have already gone out are left exactly as they were. An accepted quote or a paid invoice is a record of what was actually sold, and the school is holding a PDF that says 85 inch. Rewriting those would put our system out of step with the customer's copy, and on paid invoices that is an accounting problem. On production that is 27 lines: 7 accepted quotes, 1 expired quote, 11 part-paid invoices and 8 paid invoices.

RESULT ON PRODUCTION. 63 draft lines now read "86 Inch Interactive Board". The 27 issued lines still read 85, on purpose.

Verified on staging first against the same data: 57 of 57 draft lines followed the rename and 27 of 27 issued lines stayed put.

IF YOU WANT THE ISSUED DOCUMENTS CHANGED TOO, say so and it can be done — but it should be a deliberate decision, not something the system does quietly.

data.title: [CON1] A contact can only hold one usable phone number
data.description:
Requested by Prince 2026-07-24: "the headmasters have 2 phone numbers, there should be an option to add 2 numbers under the same person."

CURRENT STATE: a contact record has two number fields — phone and whatsapp_number — so the capacity technically exists. It is not being used:
  - 135 of 1,821 contacts have anything in the second field
  - 114 of those simply repeat the same number
  - 21 contacts in the entire CRM hold a genuinely different second number

The reason is the label. It says "WhatsApp Number", so a rep with a head who has two lines sees no place for the second one. The People tab also renders whatever is in that field as a wa.me link, so a plain second line becomes a WhatsApp link that may not work.

The Nash file confirms the need: four cells hold two numbers jammed into one field, e.g. "773465267/0714926344".

RECOMMENDED: add a separate "Alternative number" field rather than repurposing the WhatsApp one. WhatsApp already means something — it drives the wa.me link and the WhatsApp activity form — and overloading it would make the 114 existing rows ambiguous. Then show both numbers on the contact and lead views, and make the duplicate check search all of them.

Do this together with PH1, or a second number simply doubles the number of formats that fail to match.

data.title: [DUP3] The same lead can be saved twice — no guard on the create form
data.description: The same lead can be saved twice. The form does guard against a double-click and does warn about likely duplicates, but nothing stops an identical lead being created again a few minutes later.
data.resolution_note:
CORRECTION to the original text of this ticket, after reading the code and testing the duplicate peek directly.

The ticket first said the create form has no guard against a second submit. That is WRONG. create-new-lead.tsx does hold an isSubmitting flag that disables the button while a save is in flight, and the page already renders a DuplicateWarningBanner.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED (peek endpoints, tested on staging):
 - lead peek WITH a school id or phone -> correctly finds the existing lead
 - lead peek with the NAME alone -> 0 candidates
 - school peek with an EXACT name+city+province match -> 0 candidates (raised as DUP4)

So the protection that exists is advisory only: a dismissible banner that never blocks the save, and one that stays silent while the user has typed only a name — exactly when a duplicate is about to be created. The isSubmitting flag is React state, not a synchronous lock, so two submits fired before the re-render can both get through. And nothing on the SERVER rejects an identical lead.

REVISED FIX
 1. Server-side: reject, or return the existing record for, a create that exactly matches an open lead on the same school + contact. The client cannot be trusted alone.
 2. Client: make the submit guard a synchronous ref rather than state.
 3. Make the warning BLOCK on an exact match and offer to open the existing lead.
 4. Make the lead peek return candidates on a name-only match.

DATA IMPACT: three surplus leads on production, none with activities, stage or value. Cleanup is BLOCKED by R2 — DELETE /leads/:id needs admin or sales_manager and refuses admin_support (verified HTTP 403).

data.title: [SC2] Planned card will hide an OVERDUE next step once the new logic ships
data.description:
Found 2026-07-23 while testing SC1 — caught BEFORE reaching production.

The development branch changed the Planned card to select only a genuinely UPCOMING dated step (this was the correct fix for a separate problem: an undated activity being shown in a slot labelled PLANNED).

Side effect: when a lead's only dated step is OVERDUE, the new logic matches nothing and the Planned card renders EMPTY. Verified against the live Lobengula High lead, whose sole dated activity is a task due 20 Jul, now overdue — dev logic returns nothing at all for it.

An empty card is worse than a wrong one here: the rep is shown no next step precisely when they have an overdue commitment demanding attention.

Fix before shipping the dev engagement-workspace to production: select the soonest upcoming dated step; if none exists, fall back to the most overdue dated step and label it clearly as overdue. Only fall back to nothing when there is genuinely no dated commitment at all. Do NOT restore the old "newest open by created_at" fallback, which is what put undated items in the Planned slot in the first place.
data.resolution_note:
CLOSED 2026-07-23 — NOT A DEFECT. This ticket was raised in error by me (Prince's assistant) and is withdrawn.

When I raised it I simulated the development branch's planned-card logic as "upcoming dated steps only" (due_at >= now). That filter does not exist in the code. The actual implementation in engagement-workspace.tsx takes ALL open dated non-note activities, sorts ascending by date and returns the first — so an OVERDUE step is still selected and still displayed.

Verified against the live Lobengula High lead by running the real code path over the live API response:
  actual dev logic -> "Confirm with FD what terms can be offered" due 2026-07-20 (overdue) — SELECTED
  my earlier (wrong) simulation -> null / empty card
The card also renders an overdue state: ActivityStateBadge covers overdue / due today / scheduled / no due date, so the item is both shown and labelled.

Consequence: LCK1 / C9 are NOT blocked and can go to production once approved. Lesson recorded — simulate the code as written, not as summarised.

data.title: [SC1] Lead page: "Planned / Next step" disagrees with the sidebar and can show an undated item
data.description: Reported from a screenshot: the Planned and Next step panels on a lead disagreed with each other. Investigated against the live record and it behaved correctly, so nothing was changed. Raise it again with the lead name if it reappears.
data.resolution_note:
TESTED 2026-07-23 (same day) by calling the exact endpoint the Planned card calls, with the exact parameters, and simulating both client code paths against the live response.

GET /activities?lead_id=<lobengula>&open_only=true&limit=25&page=1&include_details=true
-> 200, 20 rows, and the dated task "Confirm with FD" is returned at POSITION 1.
-> Production client logic now selects it via the DATED path.

CONCLUSION: the screenshot behaviour NO LONGER REPRODUCES. The ACT1 sort fix deployed to production earlier today incidentally fixed it — under the old ordering (CASE WHEN type='task' THEN due_at ELSE NULL END DESC, which puts NULLs first) the one dated TASK was sorted to the very end of the result set; it now comes first. The screenshot was taken before that deploy.

Stated honestly: I can prove it does not reproduce now, and I can prove the ordering changed. I cannot fully prove the original mechanism after the fact, so this is closed on "does not reproduce" plus a known-relevant fix, not on a confirmed root cause.

NEW AND IMPORTANT — a separate defect found while testing, NOT yet fixed:
The development branch's replacement logic requires a genuinely UPCOMING dated step. On this lead the only dated activity is OVERDUE (20 Jul). So when the dev version of engagement-workspace ships to production, this lead's Planned card will render EMPTY — hiding an overdue commitment entirely, which is worse than showing the wrong one. An overdue next step must still be shown, and shown prominently. This MUST be fixed before that branch reaches production. Raised as SC2.

The cause was in the forms, not the team: the call form displayed a follow-up date picker but never sent the value; the meeting form had its date mapping commented out; WhatsApp and email had no date field at all. data.title: [ACT1] "All" tab buries today's activities — dated tasks sort to the last pages
data.description: The All tab on Activities buried today's work. Anything with a date sorted to the very back, so today's entries sat on page 110 of 112 while undated ones filled the front.
data.resolution_note: FIXED + LIVE ON PRODUCTION 2026-07-23. The All tab sorted dated tasks to the BACK (Postgres DESC puts NULLs first), which is why today's work sat on page 110 of 112. It now orders by the activity's effective date, newest first — today's items appear on page 1. Verified live. A new "Logged today" tab was also added, and "Today" renamed to "Due today", so "what the team recorded today" and "what is due today" are separate views.

data.title: [BRAND1] Browser tab shows "client" + default Vite favicon — set to DigiLearn CRM
data.description: The browser tab read 'client' with the default placeholder icon instead of the company name.
data.resolution_note: RESOLVED — LIVE ON PRODUCTION 2026-07-26. The browser tab now reads CRM-Digilearn with the orange-D-on-blue favicon (per Prince's spec: orange D #f97316 on blue tile #1d4ed8) instead of "client" + the default Vite icon. Commits e573125 + c4e2455; verified live on https://crm.digilearncrm.work (title tag and favicon.svg both serving).

data.title: [PROD-BOARD] [REMINDER for Mr Dube] Change/add product board 85″ -> 86″
data.description: A product renamed from 85 inch to 86 inch kept the old name everywhere it had already been used. Draft quotes and invoices now follow the rename; anything already issued keeps what the school was actually sent.

data.title: [DL1] Ki cannot download her quote on prod (Vercel Blob not configured)
data.description: Kim could not download her quotes. The system was trying to fetch the file from storage that has never been set up. Quotes are now generated and sent straight from the system, so the button works without that storage.
data.resolution_note: Fixed + LIVE on production: quotes now download as a PDF streamed straight from the server (GET /quotes/:id/pdf), so the "Download PDF" button in the quote preview works without Vercel Blob storage being configured. Reported for Ms Mpofu (Kim).

data.title: [QSYNC1] Quote↔pipeline↔deal sync + auto "needs disqualify" after 2 weeks
data.description: Every quote must appear in the pipeline and on the linked deal’s activity feed, and after 2 weeks a quote should flag/beep as needing disqualification. Today a quote only optionally links to a deal (deal_id) and updates deal value; there is NO enforced pipeline presence, NO deal-activity entry per quote, and NO 2-week disqualify automation (valid_until exists but nothing acts on it). BUILD/enhance the workflow; owner said look in code before touching (done — this is the finding).

data.title: [ASGN1] Rep-created leads must NOT auto-assign to the rep — sales manager assigns
data.description: A lead entered by a sales rep was automatically kept by that rep. It should arrive unassigned so a sales manager decides who gets it.
data.resolution_note: Fixed + verified LIVE on prod 2026-07-22: a lead entered by a sales rep is now left UNASSIGNED for a sales manager to assign (admin/sales_manager can still assign on creation). Server-authoritative — a rep cannot claim a lead even if the client tries.

data.title: [REA1] Reassign lead should capture a reason/note (regression from previous CRM)
data.description: Reassigning a lead to another rep records no reason. The lead simply moves, so nobody can see later why it changed hands.

data.title: [ESC1] Escalation must be available on Deals (currently Leads only)
data.description: A lead can be escalated for help, but a deal cannot — once it becomes a deal there is no way to raise a hand.

data.title: [LCK1] Next-step lock traps reps — cannot log interim activity when a future step exists
data.description: A rep could not log a call or note on a lead that already had a future follow-up booked — a box appeared demanding a next step and refused to go away. The rule on screen was stricter than the rule the system actually enforces, so reps were blocked for no reason.
data.resolution_note: RESOLVED — LIVE ON PRODUCTION 2026-07-26 (client build index-O-9yBQnS.js; the 07-24 full push had only updated the API, the client landed today). The Next-step modal no longer traps users: the client policy now mirrors the server's escape hatches — every non-actionable type is exempt, managers/admins are exempt, and an already-open actionable activity on the same lead/deal satisfies the requirement. When a commitment already exists the dialog names it (e.g. "Meeting: Demo walkthrough — due 6 Aug") and offers "Keep existing next step" alongside "Add another step". The hard lock still applies where the rule genuinely bites: a sales rep completing the LAST open actionable activity on an active lead/deal. Staging-verified 2026-07-23; commits 0f0b4f9 + 6985918.

data.title: [HYG1] Lead hygiene score unfairly penalises active reps (same last-touch bug family)
data.description: The lead hygiene score punishes reps unfairly. Every lead is measured against the same 'last contacted' rule regardless of its stage, so a rep working a long, patient sale scores badly for doing the right thing.

data.title: [AUD1] Audit History always empty — nothing writes to audit_logs
data.description: The Audit History tab is empty on every record, always. Nothing in the system ever writes to it, so there is currently no trail of who changed what. Note that a separate, working history does exist and is what we have been relying on.

data.title: [N5] sales_manager can read arbitrary single settings
data.description: Any sales manager could read individual system settings one at a time, even though the settings page as a whole is admin-only.
data.resolution_note: Single-key and category settings reads are admin-only, matching the bulk settings endpoint. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [N4] Quote not marked Accepted when invoiced via the Manual Invoice link
data.description: Creating an invoice from a quote using the Manual Invoice route left the quote sitting as unaccepted, while the Convert button marked it accepted. The same thing now happens whichever route is used.
data.resolution_note: Creating an invoice against a quote via Manual Invoice marks the source quote Accepted, matching Convert. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [N3] discipline-metrics uses brittle ILIKE counting
data.description: The discipline figures count activities by searching their titles for words like 'demo' and 'proposal'. Anything worded differently is missed and anything mentioning the word twice is counted twice, so the numbers are unreliable. The screen that used them is not currently in use.

data.title: [N2] Requisition self-approval (segregation-of-duties gap)
data.description: A manager can raise a cash request and then approve it themselves — there is nothing requiring a second person. That is a control gap rather than a fault: the system will let one person authorise their own money.

data.title: [N1] Collections aging report has no owner scoping
data.description: The collections ageing report was closed to sales reps entirely, and showed the whole company's unpaid instalments to everyone else. Reps can now see it, limited to the invoices they own.
data.resolution_note: The collections aging report takes an owner scope and is open to sales reps for the invoices they own. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C10] “Discard changes” does not revert the Auto-assign toggle
data.description: On the Compliance screen, pressing 'Discard changes' put every setting back except the Auto-assign switch, which quietly kept the new value.
data.resolution_note: Discard changes in Compliance & Controls also reverts the Auto-assign toggle. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C9] Next-step compliance gate makes completion impossible for reps
data.description: A rep marking any activity done on an active lead was trapped by a follow-up box they could not satisfy or dismiss, so the activity could never be closed.
data.resolution_note: RESOLVED — LIVE ON PRODUCTION 2026-07-26 (client build index-O-9yBQnS.js). Same root fix as LCK1: the client completion gate was strictly harsher than the server's assertNextStepCompliance — it ignored the admin/sales_manager bypass and the already-open-next-step hatch, so completion looked impossible in cases the server had already accepted. The client now resolves that context (caller roles + other open actionable activities on the record) before deciding whether to demand a next step, and stays permissive while the lookup is in flight. Verified on staging 2026-07-23; commits 0f0b4f9 + 6985918.

data.title: [C8] deal.value overwritten by the last quote/invoice total
data.description: A deal's value is overwritten by the total of the last quote or invoice raised against it, so a manager's own figure for the deal gets silently replaced.

data.title: [C7] False “Incomplete data” / “Not yet qualified” markers on leads
data.description: Leads were wrongly branded 'Incomplete data' and 'Not yet qualified' on the lists and board. The check was looking for qualification details that had not been loaded onto the screen, and treating 'not loaded' as 'missing'. Almost every lead past New looked like a problem.
data.resolution_note: List/kanban markers distinguish "not loaded" from "missing", and the Qualify chip is derived from lead status. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C6] Reversal-request review dialog shows blank fields
data.description: When a manager opened a request to reverse a lead's status, the review box was blank — no status, no date, no reason. The screen was looking for information under the wrong names, so it displayed nothing and the manager had to decide blind.
data.resolution_note: The reversal-request dialog and pending card read the API's real fields - requested status and dates now show. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C5] Pipeline summary KPIs are not owner-scoped while the board is
data.description: A rep's pipeline header counted the whole company's deals and value, while the board underneath showed only their own — so the numbers at the top never matched the cards below.
data.resolution_note: Pipeline header KPIs reuse the board's ownership conditions - a rep's header counts the same deals as their board. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C4] Invoice “Overdue” KPI is always 0
data.description: The 'Overdue' figure on Invoices always read zero, even with plainly overdue invoices on screen. It was counting a label that nothing in the system ever applies, instead of comparing against the due date. It now counts invoices genuinely past their due date with money still owing.
data.resolution_note: The invoice Overdue KPI is computed from due dates (unpaid, past grace/due) instead of a status nothing ever writes. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C3] Debug alert() shipped in the New-Invoice form
data.description: Choosing a payment term on the New Invoice screen popped up a box full of raw technical text and blocked the page. It was debugging output accidentally left in the shipped system.
data.resolution_note: Removed the debug alert() that popped raw JSON on the New-Invoice payment-term flow. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.

data.title: [C2] Deal activity feed corrupted for deals that came from a lead
data.description: On a deal that came from a lead, the activity tabs were wrong: Done and Planned showed the same jumble, and filters were ignored. One line of the query was breaking every filter applied after it.
data.resolution_note: The lead+deal activity OR is bracketed, so status/open/date filters apply again on lead-originated deals. Deployed to staging and production 2026-07-26 and verified live per role.
